For 2027 entry, Bath's IB offers are 35 points overall with 6,6,5 or 6,5,5 at Higher Level for Pharmacy MPharm (B230), Sociology and Social Policy, Criminology and Modern Languages BA; all other published undergraduate offers are 36 points overall, with HL grades ranging from 6,6,5 (Chemistry, Biology and Management courses) through 7,6,6 to 7,7,6 in three Higher Level subjects, including any required subjects. Computer Science asks for 7,7,6, including 6 in either HL Mathematics course; Mechanical, Aerospace and Integrated Design Engineering MEng ask for 7,7,6, including 6 in Physics and 7 in either HL Mathematics course. For Mathematics, Mathematics and Statistics, and Economics and Mathematics, you must take Mathematics: Analysis & Approaches at Higher Level (Applications & Interpretations does not count); most other quantitative courses accept either HL Mathematics course, and several also accept Standard Level AA at grade 6-7. The GCSE Mathematics requirement ranges from grade 4/C to 7/A by course, and any IB Higher or Standard Level Mathematics meets it. Bath accepts any IB Higher or Standard Level English or Mathematics in place of the corresponding essential GCSE requirement. Contextual offers vary by course, typically 6,6,6 or 7,6,5 at HL.

For 2027 entry, Exeter gives course offers as total IB points followed by the Higher Level grades. BMBS Medicine: 38/766 (HL 6 in Chemistry and HL 6 in Biology, plus UCAT or GAMSAT); BSc Economics and BSc Economics and Finance: 38/766-36/666 (HL5 or SL6 in Mathematics AA or AI; Maths Studies does not count); LLB Law and BSc Psychology: 36/666 (Psychology needs HL6 in a science subject); BSc Computer Science (HL5 Mathematics AA or AI), BSc Mathematics and BSc Mathematics with Economics (HL6 Mathematics AA only), and BSc Geography (HL5 in a science subject): 36/666-34/665. BSc Physics: 36/666-32/655 (HL6 Mathematics AA and HL5 Physics, or HL5 Mathematics AA and HL6 Physics); MEng Mechanical Engineering and MEng Renewable Energy Engineering: 34/665-32/655 (HL5 Mathematics AA or AI plus HL5 in another science subject); BA Politics, BA International Relations, BA History, BA English (HL5 in an accepted Humanities or Social Science subject) and the Business School BScs (Business and Management, Marketing and Management, Accounting and Finance; GCSE B/5 Mathematics or the A-Level Maths route): 34/665; BSc Environmental Science and BSc Exercise and Sport Sciences: 34/665-32/655 (HL5 in a science subject); BSc Biological Sciences (HL5 Biology plus HL5 in another science), BSc Biomedical Sciences (HL5 Biology plus HL5 in another accepted science), BSc Neuroscience (HL5 in two science subjects), BSc Zoology, BSc Marine Biology (HL5 in a science subject), BSc/BA Classics and BA Film & Television Studies: 32/655; BA/BSc Sociology, BSc Criminology, BA Archaeology and BA Modern Languages (language requirement depends on the level you choose): 32/655-30/555. You need GCSE grade C/4 in English Language across courses; some science and business courses also need GCSE B/5 or 6 in Mathematics (the Maths Transition Course may be an option if you are one grade below). Contextual offers are typically 2-4 points lower; Exeter gives 2022 entry as the example. Exeter intends to set the 2027/28 standard Home fee at £10,050, with an intended rate of £10,050 for each year of study; on BMBS Medicine, years one to four are at the standard rate and the NHS pays for year five if current funding arrangements continue. The published 2027/28 international fees are £25,700 for Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences (including Law), Accounting, Finance, Business & Management, Economics and Marketing; £31,500 for Computer Science, Earth and Environmental Sciences, Ecology and Conservation, Engineering, Geology, Geography, Mathematics and Statistics, Medical Imaging, Natural Sciences, Neuroscience, Nursing, Physics, and Sport and Health Sciences; £32,150 for Biosciences, Biomedical Sciences and Psychology; £49,300 for BMBS Medicine at the 2027 rate; Exeter expects modest fee increases each year of study in line with the Consumer Price Index.

Glasgow offers Scottish four-year degrees, including many MA (Hons) and MA (SocSci) programmes and BSc degrees in science and engineering; some degrees let students with strong results progress to an MSci or MEng. Glasgow gives its standard IB Diploma offers for 2027 entry by course. The standard IB entry format is NN (HL a,b,c): total points followed by Higher Level grades. The offers include 38 (6,6,6) for Computing Science, Software Engineering MEng, Mechanical/Aeronautical/Civil/Electronic & Electrical/Biomedical Engineering MEng, Medicine MBChB, Veterinary Medicine & Surgery BVMS and Psychology BSc (upper end of the Psychology range); 36 (6,6,6) for Dentistry BDS; 36 (6,6,5) for Business & Management MA (SocSci), Economics MA (SocSci), Politics MA (Hons) and Sociology MA (SocSci); 34 (6,5,5) for Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Physics with Astrophysics MPhys, Genetics, Zoology, Neuroscience and English Literature MA (Hons); 32 (5,5,5) for Chemistry and Geography BSc; 32 (6,5,5) at the lower end for History/Philosophy/Classics/French/Film & Television Studies/Archaeology MA (Hons) and International Relations MA (SocSci). Some courses give a range: Psychology runs from 38 (6,6,6 HL) down to 34 (6,5,5 HL); Scots Law LLB and International Relations give the range as 38 - 32/34. Check the HL subjects for your course: you need Mathematics (Analysis & Approaches) HL 6 for Computing Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Physics, Chemistry and all Engineering routes; HL Biology or Chemistry for Life Sciences; HL Chemistry and HL Biology plus UCAT for Medicine, Dentistry and Veterinary Medicine; HL English (or Humanities) plus LNAT for Scots Law LLB. On courses with both routes, the IB offer is 34 (6,5,5) for the BEng; for the MEng it is 38 (6,6,6). The 2026/27 standard RUK fee (England, Wales, Northern Ireland) is GBP 9,790; Glasgow has not yet published the 2027/28 RUK standard fee in its live fee information. The Scotland fee is GBP 1,820 (SAAS pays it for eligible Scottish students). International fees for 2027/28: GBP 28,275 for Arts and Social Sciences; GBP 33,708 for Science, Engineering, Nursing and College of Medical, Veterinary and Life Sciences programmes; GBP 60,255 for Bachelor of Dental Surgery (BDS); GBP 38,670 for Bachelor of Veterinary Medicine and Surgery (BVMS); GBP 67,112 for MBChB and CMVLS clinical programmes. Glasgow's live course pages show the IB offer only through the JavaScript country selector; the IB figures here come from archived Glasgow course pages for 2026/27 (Wayback snapshots from 2025-09/2025-10), as noted in the individual programme deadline notes.

For Computer Science BSc, the IB Diploma options are 36 with 6 in HL Maths; 34 with 6 in HL Maths and A in the Extended Essay; or 34 with 6 in HL Maths and 5 in HL Computer Science. The A Level options are AAA including Maths or AAB including A in Maths and B in Computer Science. The typical offer is usually one or two points higher than the alternative offer; the alternative requires grade A in the Extended Essay (or equivalent) in those cases. Examples for 2027 entry: Computer Science BSc and Computer Science (Artificial Intelligence) BSc ask for IB 36 with 6 in HL Maths, or 34 with 6 in HL Maths plus A in the EE or 5 in HL CS; Mathematics BSc and Financial Mathematics BSc ask for IB 36 with 6 in HL Maths (Analysis and Approaches), or 34 with 6 in HL Maths AA and A in the EE; Physics BSc asks for IB 34 with 6,5 in HL Maths and Physics (in either order), or 33 with 5 in HL Maths and Physics and B in the EE; Physics MPhys asks for IB 36 with 6 in HL Maths and Physics, or 34 with 6,5 and A in the EE; Chemistry BSc and MChem ask for IB 34 with 5 in HL Chemistry, or 33 with B in the EE; Biological Sciences BSc asks for IB 34 with 6,5 in HL Biology and a second science, or 33 with A in a science-based EE; Biomedical Science BSc asks for IB 34 with 6,5 in two HL science subjects; Psychology BSc asks for IB 34 with 5 in an HL science subject; Data Science BSc asks for IB 34, or 33 with A in a science-based EE; Economics BSc asks for IB 34 with 5 in HL Maths, or 33 with B in the EE; Business Management BA and Accounting and Financial Management BA ask for IB 34, or 33 with A in the EE; Law LLB asks for IB 36, or 34 with A in the EE; Medicine MBChB asks for IB 36 with 6 in three HL subjects including Chemistry or Biology and a second science, and at least 4 in all SL subjects; Dental Surgery BDS asks for IB 36 with 6 in HL Chemistry and Biology; Nursing (Adult) BMedSci asks for IB 32; Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering MEng ask for IB 38 with 6 in HL Maths and at least one of Physics/Chemistry/Biology (Mechanical also offers 36 with A in a science-based EE); Civil and Structural, Electrical and Electronic, Chemical, Materials Science and Engineering, and Mechatronic and Robotic Engineering MEng ask for IB 36 with 6 in HL Maths, or 34 with 6,5 in HL Maths and a science plus A/B in the EE; Architecture BA asks for IB 36, or 34 with A in the EE, plus a portfolio and GCSE Maths grade 4/C; Landscape Architecture BA asks for IB 33, or 32 with B in the EE, plus a portfolio; Journalism Studies BA asks for IB 33, or 32 with B in the EE; Digital Media and Society BA and Sociology BA ask for IB 33, or 32 with B in the EE; Politics and International Relations BA and Criminology BA ask for IB 34, or 33 with B in the EE; Geography BA asks for IB 34, or 33 with B in the EE; Urban Studies and Planning MPlan(UG) asks for IB 33, or 32 with B in a social-science based EE, plus GCSE Maths grade 4/C; English Literature BA asks for IB 34, or 33 with B in the EE; History BA and Philosophy BA ask for IB 34, or 33 with B in the EE; Modern Languages and Cultures BA typically asks for IB 33 with 5 in an HL modern foreign language, or 32 with B in the EE. For an IB offer with a range, you qualify for the lower end only if you meet the course's Extended Essay or additional HL grade condition. Sheffield typically asks for GCSE English Language and GCSE Maths at grade 4/C or above (some courses are higher); many Engineering and Psychology courses ask for GCSE Maths at grade 6/B or 5/B. Sheffield's 2027 fee schedule gives the published 2027/28 Home tuition fee as GBP 10,050 per year. If you start an undergraduate course in 2027 and pay Home fees, the standard annual fee is GBP 10,050.

Southampton sets its IB Diploma offer by course, giving the total Diploma points and the Higher Level points you need. For Archaeology BA, pass with 30 points overall and 15 at Higher Level; for Computer Science BSc, pass with 34 points overall and 17 at Higher Level, including 6 at Higher Level in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or 6 at Higher Level in Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation; for Electronic/Electrical/Mechanical/Aeronautics and Astronautics/Civil/Biomedical Engineering MEng, pass with 38 points overall and 19 at Higher Level, including 6 at Higher Level in Physics (or Biology/Chemistry/Computer Science) and 6 at Higher Level in Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches or Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation; for Medicine BM5 BMBS, you need 36 points overall with 18 at Higher Level, with 6 in Biology and one additional science. Under its IB Diploma rules, Southampton accepts both Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches (HL) and Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation (HL) for all undergraduate courses with IB requirements. Many Engineering/CS/Maths/Physics courses prefer Analysis and Approaches; Acoustical Engineering MEng asks for either 6 at HL in AA or 7 at HL in AI. If you lack the required HL subjects, you can apply for the Engineering/Physics/Mathematics Foundation Year. Most courses ask for GCSE English Language (or GCSE English) and GCSE Mathematics at grade 4/C or above; if you do not have GCSE English Language (or GCSE English) and GCSE Mathematics at grade 4/C or above, you can use an equivalent Southampton accepts. Southampton accepts the IB Career-Related Programme (IBCP); it bases offers on your individual Diploma Course subjects and career-related study qualification, leaving out the CP core. Eligible Home applicants can get a contextual offer; if Southampton identifies you for one, your offer will be below the typical offer for your programme. The published 2027/28 Home tuition fee is GBP 10,050 per year, the GBP 10,050 rate given for UK students on these courses.

St Andrews offers Scottish four-year degrees. For 2027 entry, each course has Standard and Minimum grades for the IB Diploma. The Standard is 38 (HL 6,6,6) for Computer Science (including HL6 Mathematics and SL5 in a listed science), Mathematics BSc/MMath, Statistics, Physics BSc/MPhys, Astrophysics MPhys (physics degrees include HL6 Mathematics and Physics), Chemistry BSc/MChem (including HL6 Chemistry and HL6 in one listed science), Geography, Sustainable Development, Economics, Financial Economics, Management, International Relations, History (including HL6 History) and English (including HL6 English); the Standard is 36 (HL 6,6,5) for Biology, Marine Biology, Biochemistry (HL6 Biology and HL6 Chemistry), Neuroscience (HL5 in two of Biology/Chemistry/Mathematics/Physics), Psychology, Classics, Art History, Social Anthropology, Film Studies, French (including French B HL6 or French A SL7) and Theological Studies. The Minimum is 36 (HL 6,5,5) across courses; Gateway programmes support contextual applicants who narrowly miss the Minimum grades. For every course you also need SQA National 5 (B)/GCSE (5) in English and one listed science or mathematics subject, or the IB equivalent. The RUK rate for 2027 entry (England, Wales, Northern Ireland, Republic of Ireland, Channel Islands and Isle of Man) is GBP 10,050 per year for the courses listed for 2027, pending confirmation by the UK Government; the Home (Scotland) fee is TBC by the Scottish Government (it was GBP 1,820 in 2025-2026, with SAAS paying for eligible Scottish students). The international (EU and overseas) fee for 2027 entry is GBP 34,910 per year for degrees in the Faculties of Arts, Divinity and Science; the Medicine fee for 2026-2027 entrants is GBP 39,620. The undergraduate courses reviewed do not require admissions tests; only Medicine, Gateway/supported pathway programmes and part-time study use interviews. Many science degrees allow well-qualified applicants to enter in second year.
